sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy sets out how the organisation responds to security incidents affecting the in-scope services, so incidents are detected, contained, resolved and learned from, supporting the SOC 2 system operations criteria.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All security incidents affecting the systems and data supporting the in-scope services.

sections.heading: 3. Incident Process
sections.body:
A documented process governs the lifecycle of an incident:
- It covers detection, reporting, triage, containment, eradication, recovery and closure.
- Roles and severity levels are defined so the response is coordinated and proportionate.
- Evidence is preserved to support investigation and any notification.

sections.heading: 4. Communication
sections.body:
Communication during an incident is defined in advance:
- Internal escalation paths and decision authority are set.
- Customer and regulator notification is made where service commitments or law require, on the required timeline.
- [FILL IN: your customer-notification commitments and timelines.]

sections.heading: 5. Post-Incident
sections.body: After a significant incident, a review captures the root cause and lessons learned, and the resulting improvements are tracked to completion.

sections.heading: 6. Testing
sections.body: The incident response process is exercised periodically (for example a tabletop) so it works when a real incident occurs.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy establishes the information security programme that underpins the organisation's SOC 2 controls, covering governance, risk, control activities, communication and monitoring, in line with the SOC 2 common criteria.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The organisation's information systems, data and the people and processes that support the in-scope services.

sections.heading: 3. Governance and Control Environment
sections.body:
Leadership establishes the environment in which controls operate:
- Leadership sets the tone for security and demonstrates a commitment to integrity and competence.
- Roles and responsibilities for security are defined, and people are held accountable for them.
- The organisational structure and reporting lines for security are clear.

sections.heading: 4. Risk Assessment
sections.body: Risks to the service commitments are identified, assessed and treated through a documented risk assessment (see the SOC 2 risk assessment), which is revisited as the business and threats change.

sections.heading: 5. Control Activities
sections.body:
Controls are selected and operated to address the assessed risks:
- Control activities, including over technology, are designed to mitigate risks to the commitments.
- They are recorded in the control matrix and mapped to the applicable criteria.
- Changes to systems and controls are managed so the control environment is not eroded.

sections.heading: 6. Communication and Monitoring
sections.body:
The programme is communicated and kept effective:
- Security commitments and responsibilities are communicated internally and to customers.
- Controls are monitored, and deficiencies are tracked to resolution.
- [FILL IN: how often the programme and controls are reviewed.]

sections.heading: 9. Compliance & Enforcement
sections.body: Compliance with this policy is mandatory. Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, and may be reported to relevant authorities where required by law.

sections.heading: 10. Exceptions
sections.body: Any exception to this policy must be requested in writing, risk-assessed, and approved by [Approver / CISO] at [Company Name]. Approved exceptions are documented, time-bound and reviewed at expiry.

sections.heading: 11. Review
sections.body: This policy is reviewed at least annually, or after a significant change or security incident, and updated as required.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy ensures security-relevant events are logged and monitored so the organisation can detect, investigate and respond to anomalies and incidents, supporting the SOC 2 system operations criteria.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The systems, applications and infrastructure supporting the in-scope services.

sections.heading: 3. Logging
sections.body:
Security-relevant activity is captured and preserved:
- Authentication, access, configuration changes and administrative actions are logged.
- Logs are protected against tampering and unauthorised access.
- Clocks are synchronised and logs are retained for a defined period.

sections.heading: 4. Monitoring and Detection
sections.body:
The environment is actively watched:
- Logs and systems are monitored for anomalies and indicators of compromise.
- Alerting is configured on defined conditions, and alerts are triaged.
- [FILL IN: name your logging and monitoring tools.]

sections.heading: 5. Vulnerability Monitoring
sections.body: Vulnerabilities are identified through scanning and other means, risk-ranked, and tracked to remediation within defined timeframes.

sections.heading: 6. Response
sections.body: Detected events are triaged and escalated to the incident response process where warranted, so detection leads to action.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy governs logical access to the organisation's systems and data, supporting the SOC 2 logical and physical access criteria, so access is restricted to authorised users and managed across its lifecycle.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All systems, applications and data supporting the in-scope services, and all user and service accounts.

sections.heading: 3. Access Provisioning
sections.body:
Access is granted in a controlled, accountable way:
- Access is granted only on documented approval, on the principle of least privilege.
- Each account is unique and attributable to an individual; shared accounts are avoided.
- Service accounts are inventoried and owned.

sections.heading: 4. Authentication
sections.body:
Accounts are protected by strong authentication:
- Strong authentication is enforced, with multi-factor authentication for remote and privileged access.
- Credential standards (length, rotation where justified, secure storage) are applied.

sections.heading: 5. Access Reviews
sections.body:
Standing access is kept correct:
- User access is reviewed at a defined frequency, and privileged access more often.
- Access is removed promptly on role change or termination.
- [FILL IN: your access-review cadence and joiner/mover/leaver process.]

sections.heading: 6. Privileged and Data Access
sections.body: Higher-risk access and data are given extra protection: privileged access is restricted and monitored, and data is protected in transit and at rest according to its classification.

sections.body: This system description sets out the boundaries of the system covered by a SOC 2 report, the service commitments and system requirements, and the controls in place. It is a required part of a SOC 2 report and the reference an assessor works from.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The infrastructure, software, people, procedures and data that deliver the in-scope services.

sections.heading: 4. Controls
sections.body: The controls that meet the applicable trust services criteria are described and recorded in the control matrix, with the evidence that demonstrates them.

sections.heading: 5. How the Description Is Used
sections.body:
The description is written for the reader of the report (a customer or their auditor), in enough detail that they understand the boundary, the commitments and the controls without seeing the environment. It is kept consistent with the control matrix and is updated when the services, boundary or commitments change, so that the description used for the report period matches what was actually in place.
